summary: Guidance covers Star India deconsolidation, with India JV expected to contribute $73 million to Entertainment and $9 million to Sports in fiscal 2025, plus a roughly $300 million full-year equity loss from purchase accounting. Q2 fiscal 2025 guidance includes a modest Disney+ subscriber decline, Sports impacts of about $100 million from college sports and one additional NFL game and about $50 million from exiting the Venu Sports JV, and Disney Cruise Line pre-opening expense of about $40 million. Fiscal 2025 guidance includes high-single-digit adjusted EPS growth, approximately $15 billion cash provided by operations, double-digit Entertainment growth with about $875 million higher DTC operating income, 13% Sports growth, 6% to 8% Experiences growth, and about $200 million Disney Cruise Line pre-opening expense; CEO Robert A. Iger highlights box office, DTC profitability, ESPN tile on Disney+, and Experiences.

title: SUMMARIZED FINANCIAL RESULTS; SUMMARIZED SEGMENT FINANCIAL RESULTS
summary: The summarized financial results table shows Q1 fiscal 2025 revenues of $24,690 million, income before income taxes of $3,660 million, total segment operating income of $5,060 million, diluted EPS of $1.40, adjusted EPS of $1.76, cash provided by operations of $3,205 million, and free cash flow of $739 million. The summarized segment results show Entertainment revenue of $10,872 million and operating income of $1,703 million, Sports revenue of $4,850 million and operating income of $247 million, Experiences revenue of $9,415 million and operating income of $3,110 million, and eliminations of $(447) million.

title: DISCUSSION OF FIRST QUARTER SEGMENT RESULTS

nodes.title: Star India
nodes.summary: On November 14, 2024, The Walt Disney Company and Reliance Industries Limited completed the Star India Transaction to form an India joint venture combining Star-branded channels and the Disney+ Hotstar service with certain RIL media and entertainment businesses. RIL holds an effective 56% controlling interest, the Company holds 37%, and a third-party investment company holds 7%, with the Company recognizing its 37% share in Equity in the income of investees after the transaction.

nodes.title: Entertainment
nodes.summary: Entertainment revenue increased 9% to $10,872 million and operating income increased 95% to $1,703 million, driven by improved Content Sales/Licensing and Other and Direct-to-Consumer results, partially offset by lower Linear Networks results. Direct-to-Consumer revenue rose 9% to $6,072 million and operating income improved to $293 million from a loss of $138 million, with 124.6 million total Disney+ subscribers, 53.6 million total Hulu subscribers, and average monthly revenue per paid subscriber of $7.55 for Disney+ and $12.52 for Hulu SVOD Only. Content Sales/Licensing and Other revenue rose 34% to $2,183 million and operating income improved to $312 million from a loss of $224 million, reflecting Moana 2 and Mufasa: The Lion King versus The Marvels and Wish.

nodes.title: Sports
nodes.summary: Sports revenue was flat at $4,850 million, while operating income improved to $247 million from a loss of $103 million, with ESPN domestic revenue up 9% to $4,422 million and domestic operating income down 9% to $231 million. The domestic decline reflected expanded college football programming rights, including one additional College Football Playoff game, while international ESPN operating loss narrowed to $(3) million from $(56) million and Star India operating income improved to $9 million from a loss of $315 million. ESPN+ paid subscribers were 24.9 million, down 3%, and average monthly revenue per paid subscriber increased 7% to $6.36.

nodes.title: Experiences
nodes.summary: Experiences revenue increased 3% to $9,415 million and operating income was comparable at $3,110 million, with Domestic Parks and Experiences operating income down 5% to $1,982 million due to Hurricanes Milton and Helene and Disney Cruise Line pre-opening expenses. International Parks and Experiences operating income increased 28% to $420 million on higher guest spending and attendance, while Consumer Products revenue declined 2% to $1,337 million and operating income increased 1% to $708 million.

summary: This section discusses the Star India Transaction and the first quarter segment results for Entertainment, Sports, and Experiences. It presents revenue and operating income tables, explains drivers such as Moana 2, Disney+ and Hulu subscriber metrics, ESPN college football rights, and hurricane impacts, and notes the accounting change after the India joint venture was formed.

title: OTHER FINANCIAL INFORMATION

nodes.title: Corporate and Unallocated Shared Expenses; Restructuring and Impairment Charges
nodes.summary: Corporate and unallocated shared expenses increased $152 million to $460 million from $308 million, primarily due to a legal settlement. The Company also recorded a $143 million loss in connection with the Star India Transaction.

nodes.title: Interest Expense, net; Equity in the Income of Investees; Income Taxes
key_items: Equity in the Income of Investees
nodes.summary: Interest expense, net was $(367) million compared with $(246) million, driven by lower average rates and debt balances partially offset by lower capitalized interest and lower interest, investment, and other income. Equity in the income of investees decreased to $92 million from $181 million, including a $33 million loss from the India joint venture and lower A+E Television Networks income. The effective income tax rate rose to 27.8% from 25.1% due to a non-cash tax charge related to the Star India Transaction.

nodes.title: Noncontrolling Interests; Cash from Operations
nodes.summary: Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests decreased to $(90) million from $(240) million, primarily due to the prior-year comparison to accretion of NBC Universal's interest in Hulu. Cash provided by operations increased $1,020 million to $3,205 million from $2,185 million, while free cash flow decreased to $739 million from $886 million due to higher investments in parks, resorts, and other property.

nodes.title: Capital Expenditures; Depreciation Expense
nodes.summary: Capital expenditures, shown as investments in parks, resorts, and other property, increased to $2,466 million from $1,299 million, primarily due to higher spend on cruise ship fleet expansion at the Experiences segment. Depreciation expense increased to $909 million from $823 million, with Experiences depreciation of $652 million and Corporate depreciation of $82 million.

summary: Other financial information covers corporate and unallocated shared expenses, restructuring and impairment charges, interest expense, equity in the income of investees, income taxes, noncontrolling interests, cash from operations, capital expenditures, and depreciation expense. It highlights a $143 million Star India Transaction loss, a $460 million corporate expense increase, a $367 million net interest expense, a 27.8% effective tax rate, $3,205 million cash provided by operations, $2,466 million capital expenditures, and $909 million depreciation expense.

title: THE WALT DISNEY COMPANY CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED STATEMENTS OF INCOME (unaudited; $ in millions, except per share data)
summary: The condensed consolidated statements of income report Q1 fiscal 2025 revenues of $24,690 million, costs and expenses of $20,612 million, restructuring and impairment charges of $143 million, net income of $2,644 million, and net income attributable to The Walt Disney Company of $2,554 million. Diluted EPS was $1.40 and basic EPS was $1.41, with income before income taxes of $3,660 million and income taxes of $1,016 million.

title: THE WALT DISNEY COMPANY CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED BALANCE SHEETS (unaudited; $ in millions, except per share data)
summary: The condensed consolidated balance sheets report total assets of $197,046 million at December 28, 2024, compared with $196,219 million at September 28, 2024, including cash and cash equivalents of $5,486 million, receivables of $13,767 million, produced and licensed content costs of $32,505 million, goodwill of $73,312 million, and total equity of $106,739 million. The accompanying cash flow statement shows cash provided by operations of $3,205 million, cash used in investing activities of $(2,575) million, cash used in financing activities of $(997) million, and ending cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash of $5,582 million.

title: DTC PRODUCT DESCRIPTIONS AND KEY DEFINITIONS
summary: This section defines DTC product offerings, including Disney+, ESPN+, Hulu SVOD Only, and Hulu Live TV + SVOD, and explains how paid subscribers are counted for standalone, multi-product, and wholesale arrangements. It defines International Disney+ as service outside the U.S. and Canada and describes how average monthly revenue per paid subscriber is calculated, including subscription fees, advertising, premium and feature add-on revenue, and extra member add-on revenue while excluding Pay-Per-View revenue.

title: NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES
summary: The non-GAAP measures section presents diluted EPS excluding certain items, total segment operating income, and free cash flow, with reconciliations to the most comparable GAAP measures. Adjusted EPS of $1.76 excludes a $143 million restructuring and impairment charge and $397 million of TFCF and Hulu intangible asset amortization and fair value step-up, while total segment operating income of $5,060 million reconciles income before income taxes by adding corporate expenses, the India joint venture loss, restructuring charges, interest expense, and amortization. Free cash flow of $739 million is calculated as $3,205 million of cash provided by operations less $2,466 million of investments in parks, resorts, and other property.
